claim: For the reduced two-spin-qutrit Hamiltonian written by Zhang and Li, \[H=K(\mathbf S_1\!\cdot\!\mathbf S_2)^2+B(S_{1z}+S_{2z}),\qquad K<0,\]at every positive temperature \(T\), define \(r=e^{-3K/T}=e^{3|K|/T}\), \(b=B/T\), \(a=(r-1)/3\), and \(Z'=(1+2\cosh b)^2+r-1\). Its exact negativity is \[\mathcal N=\frac{2(\sqrt{\sinh^2 b+a^2}-\cosh b)+(\sqrt{\sinh^2(2b)+a^2}-\cosh(2b))}{Z'}\]when \(r>4\), and \(\mathcal N=0\) when \(r\le4\). Hence \[T_c=\frac{3|K|}{\log4}\]is the exact positive-temperature negativity threshold, independent of every finite uniform field \(B\). For \(0<T<T_c\), \(\mathcal N>0\) for every finite \(B\), so there is no finite positive-temperature critical magnetic field. At \(T=0\) only, the ground state changes from the maximally entangled spin singlet to a fully polarized product state at \(|B|=3|K|/2\). The correct spectrum has singlet energy \(4K\), while the eight-dimensional complement has energies \(K+BM\), \(M=-2,-1,0,1,2\), with multiplicities \(1,2,2,2,1\). This corrects the non-total-spin eigenvalues printed in the source and its resulting finite-field disappearance claim.

correctness.rationale: The total-spin decomposition fixes the spectrum, and partial transpose reduces to three 2x2 blocks with determinant 1-[(r-1)/3]^2. This proves the iff threshold and finite-field nonvanishing; direct 9x9 matrix replay agrees.
